brief: UBS's 2027-28 outlook: AI infrastructure build-out has offset tariff and energy drags and is driving over half of global trade growth and a large share of global GDP growth, but the outlook hinges on that build-out continuing and some Middle East de-escalation; data-centre opposition is a delay risk and enterprise AI adoption stays narrow. UBS expects progressively more disinflation into 2027, only modest further rate tightening, then a 2028 reversal of the hikes, and favours Nasdaq over Russell 2000, US curve steepeners over European flatteners, and long gold/long JPY. The rest of the note is a sales digest of separate one-liners, not one argument: US equities face a technical retest this week, but positioning (prime-brokerage long/short, CTA and risk-control exposure all near 1-year lows, short interest above the 90th percentile) sets up an asymmetric rebound once residual forced selling clears; US CPI (Tue) and Nvidia earnings (Nov 17) are the next catalysts after Thursday's record 365bn systematic sell flow rotated money from Tech into credit. China's CPI cooled to 0.7% y/y while PPI accelerated to 5.7%. APAC tech, down 39% quarter to date, gets a valuation-driven improving risk/reward call despite $312bn of forecast 2027 negative hyperscaler free cash flow.
